Subject: Data transfer mechanisms & DPF follow-up

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we start the procurement review, LegalOps has asked for a deeper write-up on how Redwood approaches cross-border transfers for customer data (specifically product inference request metadata and logs). Can you confirm the following scenarios for us with examples and references to docs: 

- Primary mechanisms you lean on for EU -> US transfers (SCCs, EU-US DPF, other contractual safeguards)
- How you layer technical controls (customer-managed KMS / BYOK, regional routing, data residency pins)
- How model caching/KV cache impacts residency obligations (do cached tokens leave the EU?)
- Subprocessor list and how you represent limited processing in the DPA annex
- Retention/ops logs: retention windows, access controls, and how audit logs are exported for customer audits

Can you send a consolidated response and any evidence packages (DPA annex template, DPF evidence pack, subprocessor list)? We’d like to share the materials with our privacy team by next Wednesday.

Best,
Samir

Globex Corporation

Subject: Re: Data transfer mechanisms & DPF follow-up

Thanks Samir — we can definitely provide a consolidated pack. High level answer first, then we'll attach the DPF evidence and DPA annex draft: 

- Mechanisms: Redwood supports standard SCCs (2021 module), plus we provide an EU-US Data Protection Framework supplementary mapping where customers require it. For regulated customers we also offer Dedicated/Private deployment options to avoid cross-border processing entirely.
- Technical controls: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK via KMS integrations), region pinning at request-routing layer, and optional per-customer caching scoping.
- KV cache and residency: by default KV cache is colocated with the serving region for performance; we can disable cross-region cache replication for EU-only residency customers.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a published subprocessor list; we'll include the current PDF export.
- Logs & retention: operational logs are retained per our retention policy (30/90/365 day bands depending on log type); we can provide audit exports and log schema to support audits.

I'll loop in Karthik for the technical mapping and Ben for the DPA annex language. Expect the evidence bundle as attachments in a follow-up. Would a 30-minute call on Tues 8 Jun to walk LegalOps through the pack work?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
VP, Legal & Privacy (Security & Compliance)
Redwood Inference

Hi Samir / Kim — technical supplement below (short). Attaching a one-page export controls summary for your internal use. Attachment: redwood_internal_export_controls_summary.pdf

1) Transfer mechanisms: Redwood signs SCCs (controller->processor modules) and provides an annex mapping to the EU-US DPF where customers request supplemental safeguards. For our hosted API we treat inference request metadata as processor-controlled metadata; the contractual approach remains SCCs + Supplementary Mapping.

2) BYOK / KMS: We integrate with major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Customers can bring keys for encryption-at-rest of model artifacts and persistent caches. Note: BYOK for ephemeral in-memory KV cache requires a dedicated/private deployment for full key separation.

3) Routing & residency: Routing policies operate at the request layer — you can pin all requests from a customer to EU-serving endpoints. For hybrid routing we support fallback to closest region but can disable cross-region fallback for regulated customers.

4) KV cache behavior: The token/KV cache used for model context is stored in the serving region. Short-lived artifacts (per-request caches) do not replicate outside the region unless a customer has explicitly enabled cross-region burst capacity.

5) Logs & audit: Access logs (who/when) and system logs (runtime traces) are logically separated; we can provide exports and scoping filters. Our standard retention bands are documented; for contractual commitments we offer custom retention schedules on Dedicated/Private plans.

If you want, I can prepare an example clause text for the DPA annex noting the BYOK caveat and cache scoping.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

- Can we see an example DPA annex clause that commits to no cross-border cache replication unless expressly permitted?

We’d like the consolidated evidence pack and DPA annex language before our internal review on Wed. Also please include any standardized playbooks you use to onboard EU-only customers.

Samir — attached are the consolidated items for Globex: DPF-evidence-pack-Globex.zip (contains our DPF mappings, encryption architecture diagram, access control matrix, and redaction/caching notes), DPA-Annex-Redwood-v1.2.docx (draft annex with explicit no-cross-border-cache-replication clause), and subprocessor-list-202706.pdf.

Short answers to LegalOps’ bullets: 

- DPF-only: Redwood will accept EU-US DPF as a standalone framework for customers that do not require SCCs, provided the customer accepts the DPF mappings and supplemental technical measures in our evidence pack. For customers wanting both, we can execute SCCs with our DPA annex (common for enterprise engagements).

- No cross-border cache replication clause: included. We’ve provided language that commits to region-scoped caching unless the customer enables cross-region burst. Sample text in annex: "Redwood will not replicate context or persistent cache data to regions outside the EU without Customer written consent; transient performance caches tied to global CDN services are excluded as described in the annex."

- BYOK: In hosted plans we support BYOK for persistent storage and model artifacts via cloud KMS integrations; however, cryptographic separation for ephemeral in-memory caches requires Dedicated or Private deployments for full assurance. The annex includes a BYOK matrix by deployment type.

- Subprocessors: the attached PDF lists subprocessors and processing locations; as of this export, no subprocessors decrypt customer inference payloads outside the EU for EU-only tenancy. We publish the list and provide 30-day notice for changes.

Next steps: 
- I’ve scheduled a 30-minute walkthrough for Tue 8 Jun 10:00 CET (invite sent).
- Please review the attachments and send any redlines to legal@redwood.com. If LegalOps needs a bespoke clause, Ben will coordinate.

Regards,
Kim
